destaque.oQueAconteceu:
The OTAN agreed to send an advanced warning aircraft (AWACS) to Poland, strengthening the alliance's air surveillance on its eastern flank. The announcement was made after the detonation of three Russian Kh‑101 missiles on Polish territory, which heightened security concerns in the region. The deputy minister of defence of Poland confirmed the decision in a statement to the press. The measure will be discussed in detail in the coming weeks, including possible additional reinforcements of Poland's air defences.

The missile incidents occur in the context of Russia's war in Ukraine, which has generated recurring tensions between OTAN and Moscow. The presence of an AWACS in Poland aims to improve early detection of air threats and serve as a deterrent element against new aggressions.
destaque.dataDoFatoObs: The OTAN decision was announced on 23/11/2026 and reported again on 24/11/2026.
destaque.porQueImporta: The deployment of an AWACS to Poland represents a significant boost to OTAN's surveillance capability on the eastern border, signalling that the alliance is ready to respond to air threats coming from Russia. This move could raise tension in relations between OTAN and Moscow, influencing the security dynamics in Europe and possibly affecting defence decisions of other member countries.
